Lesson or instruction: Use short plain sentences in the report and the push. No filler.
Improve the routine continuously without being asked. Record every lesson here and every change in the Changelog. The owner can edit or retire any row on this tab.
Rules are plain English plus your judgment. There are no Gmail filters or search queries in the Rules tab; never add one. Judge each thread against the rule text.
The owner does not want to re-approve what they already approved. When you reword or merge rules, carry the approval over and say so in Why; only genuinely new scope is proposed.

Which rule ID to log: when a specific rule fits in full (Promo, Receipts, a past event, an older recap), log that rule; when only the catch-all lets the thread go, log the catch-all. The label follows the kind of mail.

Human support tickets and relayed conversations (a support desk, a marketplace or seller message) are not marketing or receipts even when Gmail files them under Promotions or Purchases. An account warning in the Purchases category (a dormancy fee, a failed charge) is an open ask, not a receipt.

A bill-ready or statement notice is an open ask (R1), not routine bill mail, when the inbox also holds a recent ask to set up autopay for the same account: that bill will not pay itself. Show the amount and the due date.

Mail the owner's own automations send to them (digests, reports, notes to self) is not this routine's recap and not a person waiting. Archive it at the first run and put its headline numbers in the flag line so the recap shows them once.

Bounce notices for mail the owner sent: a mailer-daemon 'Delay' notice is archived and flagged once with the address and when Gmail gives up. A final 'Delivery failed' or 'Address not found' notice is an open ask (the person never got the mail): list it under Needs you until the owner resends or 7 days pass. First search Sent for a later message with the same subject to another address; if there is one, the ask is done: archive the bounce to Auto/Done and flag it once with both addresses.

search_threads results over about 65k characters are saved to a file; smaller pages arrive inline and are expensive. Use pageSize 50 and parse with jq or python via Bash. get_message on marketing mail is 10k+ tokens, so use it only when needed.

Use search_threads with view THREAD_VIEW_METADATA_ONLY when you only need IDs, senders and labels; it is about 5x smaller. The scan and unsubscribe discovery can be delegated to read-only subagents that write a TSV or JSON file; this keeps the main context small.
When many rows go into one write, rows can be dropped. Write at most 50 rows per call, compare updatedRows with the number sent, and diff column A against the source list before moving on.

Before appending to ANY tab (Rules, Unsubscribe, Playbook, Changelog, Archive log), read a small tail range (about 8 rows around the expected end) and take the row after the last one that holds values. Never work out the next row by counting rows from an earlier full read, and never read a whole column of the Archive log.
If a Sheets write returns 'service is currently unavailable', re-read the tail first; retry only if nothing was written.

The permission check sometimes blocks individual label_thread or unlabel_thread calls in an unattended run. Do not retry or work around a blocked call. Leave that thread in the inbox, do not log it as archived, show it in the Inbox tab as 'Archive blocked' with the rule ID, and list it under Problems.
Archiving about 100 threads in one run worked with no permission blocks when label_thread and unlabel_thread calls were issued in groups of about 26 (13 labels plus 13 unlabels per group).

Two runs can overlap (a late firing plus the on-time one). Before any write, re-read the tail of the tab. If the Archive log already has rows dated today from another run and a recap was sent in the last 3 hours, this run is a duplicate: apply the rules only to mail that arrived since, update the Inbox tab, skip proposals, discovery and the recap, and send a push that says so.

When another run is still working and has not sent its recap yet, wait for it. Signs: the Archive log tail has rows from the last hour that this run did not write, the INBOX count drops while you scan, or scanned threads already carry an Auto label with no INBOX. Then do not archive, log or write to any tab. Check every 5 minutes for its recap in Sent. Once the recap is there, follow the row above (this run is the duplicate). Take over from step 6 only if there is no recap and no change on any tab for 20 minutes.

Discovery can be incremental: when the previous run did the full 30-day sweep, search only mail since then (newer_than:2d). Do the full 30-day sweep once a week. Exclude monitoring senders from the keyword search: alert mail often contains the word unsubscribe.

Discovery must not rely on the English word 'unsubscribe' or on Gmail's categories alone. If the owner gets mail in other languages, add their footer words to the keyword search (for example "annulla iscrizione", "darse de baja", "se désabonner", abbestellen). Match senders that put an ID in the address (name+d123-s456@example.com) by the part before the + and the domain, and put them on the existing row.

In an unattended run the permission check can refuse the browser, even its very first call. Make one tabs_context call before preparing any browser work and count it as the one try: if it is refused, stop, leave every approve and manual row as it is, and say so under Problems. Do not fall back to WebFetch.

How to unsubscribe in the browser. (1) Hand link extraction to a read-only subagent: for rows with no stored link it reads the sender's newest email and writes the footer unsubscribe URL to a file. (2) Open each link, take a screenshot, and click by coordinates; clicks by element reference do nothing on some pages (Customer.io). Many links (Braze, Iterable, SendGrid, Klaviyo) unsubscribe on open with no click. (3) Only click; never type into a form (leave it manual), never change settings inside a signed-in account, reject optional cookies. (4) Plain http links show an error page: leave them manual. (5) At most two round trips per sender, then leave it manual with a note. (6) Write 'done' only with the confirmation text seen. One browser_batch call with navigate, wait and get_page_text handles about two senders.

WebFetch cannot open most marketing unsubscribe links: very long tracked URLs are rejected and many sites block automated requests. When discovering a sender, store the shortest untracked unsubscribe URL you can find; a click-tracker link that carries the real address in a parameter can be stored decoded.

Every run, check the senders marked done. If marketing from one arrives 3 or more days after its Done date and the browser is reachable, redo it with the footer link of the newest email and keep Status=done with the new date and a note; otherwise set it back to manual with the newest link in column E. Customer.io links switch off one topic only: on the first pass also open /manage_subscription_preferences/<token>/en on the same host and switch off every marketing topic.

On a consent or preferences page, a sender is done only when every option that covers promotional email is off. Read the text of each option that stays on: a loyalty or membership consent often includes promotional email. Do not switch such a consent off (it can end the membership and its benefits): leave the row manual, say which option is still on and what switching it off would cost, and let the owner decide.

An unsubscribe covers one recipient address. When a done sender still sends, but to a different address of the owner's (a +alias or a forwarded account), do not redo it on your own: add a proposed row that names the address and say so in the report.

Do not retry a manual row in the browser when its note names a limit that has not changed (a plain http link, a form to type in, a setting inside a signed-in account, no link at all). Retry only when a newer email from that sender offers a different link, or when the owner asks.
